newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's mortgage bank issues $28.4 mln bonds.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's mortgage bank issues $28.4 mln bonds.

text.p: Morocco's Credit Immobilier et Hotelier, issued 250 million dirhams ($28.4 million) bonds in five year state-guaranteed debenture bonds at a rate of 10 percent.
The bank which is listed on the Casablanca Bourse, announced the bond issue in newspapers on Thursday.
The bonds are guaranteed unconditionally by the state and carry an interest rate of 10 percent. The par value of the bond is 100,000 dirhams.

CIH has 65 percent of the Moroccan mortgage market but is heavily exposed to indebted state-run hotels, which have been forced to reschedule their debts to the banks after a bad tourism season in 1994.
CIH new bonds issue brought to 1.05 billion dirhams in debentures since March this year.
The bank is on a list of 114 state enterprises to be privatised by end 1998. The state owns a majority stake in CIH.
CIH last traded on Dec 16 at 188 dirhams.
